info.title: organox
info.description:
Business administration for a small or medium enterprise (stock and supplies). Single-tenant.

**Authentication**: except `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, every route requires the `session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). Without it, routes return `401`.

**Errors**: all error responses use `application/problem+json` (RFC 7807). A `429` also includes the `Retry-After` header in seconds.

**Decimals**: always transmitted as **strings** (`"1500.50"`, `"12.5"`), never numbers, to avoid losing precision.

get.summary: Accounts payable report across every supplier with an open position.
get.description:
Lists suppliers whose `balance != 0` or `unapplied_credit != 0`, ordered by
highest balance first, with open-purchase aging buckets computed from each
purchase's completion date (`0-30`, `31-60`, `61-90`, `90+`). `items` is
bounded with `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset`
(default 0), while totals, aging, and `items_total` always describe the
whole report.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of suppliers to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Suppliers to skip from the first (default 0).

200.description: Open supplier positions and aging buckets

get.summary: Accounts receivable report across customers with an open position.
get.description:
Lists customers whose `balance != 0` or `unapplied_credit != 0`, ordered by
highest balance first, with open-sale aging buckets computed from each
sale's completion date (`0-30`, `31-60`, `61-90`, `90+`). `items` is
bounded with `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset`
(default 0), while totals, aging, and `items_total` always describe the
whole report.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of customers to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Customers to skip from the first (default 0).

200.description: Open customer positions and aging buckets

post.summary: Log in.
post.description:
Returns the `session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) and the user.

`429` means the account is locked after failed attempts; includes
`Retry-After` with the remaining seconds.

post.summary: End the session on the server, not just the client.

get.summary: Authenticated user in the current request.

post.summary: Change the current user's password.
post.description:
Requires the current password. The new one must satisfy the password rule.
Every previous session of the user — including the caller's — is revoked
atomically and replaced with a rotated `session` cookie.

`429` means the account or IP is temporarily throttled after failed
attempts; includes `Retry-After` with the remaining seconds.

204.description: Password changed, previous sessions revoked and caller session rotated

401.description: Wrong current password or no session

429.description: Account locked or IP rate limit exceeded

get.summary: List customers, newest first is not the order: alphabetical by name.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Include deactivated customers. Absent, the list shows only active ones.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the name or the document, case-insensitively.

post.summary: Register a customer.
post.description:
`tax_id` is optional and unique when present; a duplicate returns 409.
`credit_limit` is optional too: absent or `null` means unlimited, `0`
means cash only, and a negative or three-decimal value is a 422.

409.description: Document is already in use

get.summary: Customer details.

patch.description:
A text field left out is not touched and cannot be cleared: there is no
body that removes a document, an email or a phone. `credit_limit` is the
one exception — an explicit `null` returns the customer to unlimited —
because it is the only field a real case has asked to clear.

409.description: Document is already in use, account is busy, or deactivating a customer with an open balance or unapplied credit

get.summary: Customer account statement.
get.description:
Returns ledger entries oldest first with their running balance, the
customer's current balance and unapplied credit (`U`), and every sale that
still owes money — all read from one consistent snapshot. Entries are
bounded with `limit` (default 100, clamped to 1..=500) and `offset`
(default 0), while `entries_total` always reports the whole ledger.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 100, clamped to 1..=500).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the oldest (default 0).

get.summary: Manual debt adjustment write log for one customer, newest first.
get.description:
Accepts `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset` (default 0)
to page through the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the newest (default 0).

200.description: Manual adjustments recorded for this customer

post.summary: Record a manual debt adjustment on a customer's account.
post.description:
Writes `adjustment_in` or `adjustment_out` without touching any wallet.
Both directions require the balance to stay `>= 0`: an adjustment may
load an opening balance or correct a debt, never create or consume
available credit.

409.description: The customer account is busy, retry

422.description: Blank note, invalid amount, or adjustment crossing zero

post.summary: Hand collected credit back to a customer through a wallet movement.
post.description:
One request, one transaction: an `account_payment_refund` outflow leaves
the method's wallet and a `credit_refund` entry moves the customer's
balance toward zero. Refused unless `amount <= unapplied_credit` and
`balance + amount <= 0`. An optional idempotency key returns the first
refund with `200` instead of handing money back twice.

200.description: Existing credit refund returned for a repeated idempotency key; nothing was written

201.description: Credit refunded: the wallet movement and ledger entry are written together

409.description: Busy customer account, or idempotency key already used by another entry kind

422.description: Unknown or inactive payment method, blank note, invalid amount, or amount exceeding available credit

post.summary:
Soft deletion. Idempotent. Never deletes: history points at the customer.
Refused with `409` while the customer carries a non-zero balance or
unapplied credit.

409.description: Customer carries an open balance or unapplied credit, or the account is busy

get.summary: Collection write log for one customer, newest first.
get.description:
Accepts `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset` (default 0)
to page through the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the newest (default 0).

post.summary: Collect money against a customer's account.
post.description:
One request, one transaction: the money enters a wallet as a single
`account_payment` movement carrying the customer and the method, and the
customer's ledger records one receipt linked to it. The allocations are the
operator's — the server never invents or applies them — and the money no
allocation consumes becomes the customer's usable credit. An optional
idempotency key makes a retry return the first receipt with `200` instead
of collecting twice.

200.description: Existing receipt returned for a repeated idempotency key; nothing was written

201.description: Money collected: the wallet movement and the receipt are written together

404.description: Unknown customer, or an allocation names an unknown sale

409.description: The customer account is busy, retry

422.description: Unknown or inactive payment method, a non-positive, too precise or too large amount, or allocations beyond what the sales owe

get.summary: List payment methods with the wallet each one pays into.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description:
Include deactivated rows. The settings screen needs them so a wallet can
be brought back; the POS does not.

post.summary: Create a payment method pointing at a wallet.
post.description:
This is the endpoint that makes a new method a data change instead of a
deploy.

409.description: Name is already in use

patch.summary: Rename, re-point or (de)activate a payment method.
patch.description:
Re-pointing changes where future money lands. Movements already recorded keep
the wallet they hit: the ledger is history, not a live join.

404.description: Payment method or wallet not found

409.description: Name is already in use

post.summary:

post.summary: Record a stock movement.
post.description:
`quantity` is always positive; `reason` determines the sign. An outflow

409.description: Insufficient stock

422.description: Invalid input or service without stock

get.summary: List purchases newest first with optional status and supplier filters.

post.summary: Open or reuse the current operator's draft purchase.

get.summary: Purchase details including its items and calculated or frozen total.

post.summary: Cancel a draft purchase. Completed purchases cannot be cancelled.

409.description: Purchase is already closed

post.summary: Complete a draft purchase: record stock inflows and cash wallet outflows atomically.

404.description: Purchase, supplier or product not found

409.description: Purchase is closed, supplier is inactive, or product is a service

422.description: Missing supplier, empty purchase, or invalid payments

post.summary: Add a product to a draft purchase (sums quantity and updates unit_cost if already present).

409.description: Purchase is closed, product is inactive, or product is a service

put.summary: Replace quantity and unit cost of an item in a draft purchase.

409.description: Purchase is closed

delete.summary: Remove an item from a draft purchase.

409.description: Purchase is closed

get.summary:
Returnable lines, open payable, wallet refund capacity, and issued returns
for one purchase.

post.summary: Return part or all of a completed purchase to its supplier.
post.description:
Deducts returned goods from stock (rejecting with 409 when stock is
insufficient), cancels open payable debt on the purchase first, and settles
any already-paid surplus according to `surplus_mode`: either refunding into
the wallets that paid for the purchase (`wallet_refund`) or leaving it as
unapplied supplier credit (`supplier_credit`).

200.description: Existing purchase return returned for a repeated idempotency key

409.description: Purchase not completed, quantity or total exceeds purchase, insufficient stock, insufficient wallet refund capacity, inactive supplier for credit, or busy supplier account

422.description: Invalid reason, idempotency key, product not in purchase, duplicate product, or invalid quantity

put.summary: Attach or clear the supplier on a draft purchase.

409.description: Purchase is closed or supplier is inactive

get.summary: One page of completed sales, most recent first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of sales to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Sales to skip from the newest (default 0).

post.summary: Open a sale draft, or return the one already open.
post.description:
A user has **one** draft at a time: reloading the sale screen does not
create new carts.

get.summary: Sale with its items and server-calculated total.

post.summary: Cancel a draft. Does not touch the stock ledger, because it never did.

409.description: Sale is no longer editable

post.summary: Complete the sale.
post.description:
In one transaction: validate stock with the product row locked, check that
the payments plus the optional `on_account` amount add up to the total,
authorize the on-account part against the customer's activity and credit
limit, write an outflow movement per item, a money movement per payment
and, when part of the total is on account, the charge in the customer's
ledger — which their available credit then pays, oldest receipt first, up
to the charged part — then close the sale. Any rejection leaves **no**
movements, no ledger entry and no status change.

409.description: Insufficient stock, sale already closed, busy customer account, or an on-account amount beyond the customer's credit limit (the remaining credit is named in the message)

422.description: Sale empty, wrong sum, unusable method, or an on-account amount without an active customer

get.summary:
The credits of a sale: what was charged, what came back and where the money
of each note went. A draft has no stored total, so the charged lines decide
it; the refunded total is the sum of the notes already issued, and
`refundable_total` is the money allowance create still enforces
(`sale_total − refunded_total`). Quantities and money can run out together:
once the allowance reaches zero, further notes are refused even if units
remain.

post.summary: Return part or all of a charged sale.
post.description:
Creates a credit note: the goods rejoin stock and the money leaves the
wallets that received the payment, in proportion to it. The sale is never
edited; a sale can be returned in several notes, but the total returned per
product can never exceed what was sold and the refunds can never exceed
what the sale charged. An optional idempotency key makes a retry return the
original note with 200 instead of issuing a duplicate.

200.description: Existing credit note returned for a repeated idempotency key

409.description: Sale not completed, more than what can still be returned, or refunds that would cross what the sale charged; the detail names the money allowance left

422.description: Invalid reason, key, line or quantity

put.summary: Attach or clear the sale's customer. Draft-only.
put.description:
`customer_id` is required in the body; `null` clears the customer. A closed
sale is a fact and takes no customer (409). The customer must exist (404) and
be active (409): those are the customers module's rules, not a copy in sales.

409.description: Sale is closed, or the customer is deactivated

post.summary: Add a product to the draft. If already present, add the quantity.
post.description: Returns the recalculated sale: the client does not add anything.

409.description: Sale is already closed

422.description: Invalid quantity or item is a service

put.summary: Set an item's quantity. Quantity 0 removes it.

409.description: Sale is already closed

delete.summary: Remove an item from the draft.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Include deactivated suppliers. Absent, only active suppliers are returned.

post.summary: Register a supplier.
post.description:
`tax_id` is optional and unique when present; a duplicate returns 409.
`credit_limit` is optional: absent or `null` means unlimited, `0` means cash only.

409.description: Document is already in use

get.summary: Supplier details with derived account balance and available credit.

patch.description:
`credit_limit` is tri-state: omitted leaves it unchanged, explicit `null`
clears it back to unlimited, and a value sets the cap. Deactivating with
`is_active: false` requires a zero account position (otherwise 409).

409.description: Document in use, open account position, or account busy

get.summary: Supplier account statement.
get.description:
Returns ledger entries oldest first with their running balance, the
supplier's current balance and unapplied credit, and every completed
purchase with an open payable — all read from one consistent snapshot.
Entries are bounded with `limit` (default 100, clamped to 1..=500) and
`offset` (default 0), while `entries_total` always reports the whole ledger.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 100, clamped to 1..=500).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the oldest (default 0).

get.summary: Manual payable adjustment write log for one supplier, newest first.
get.description:
Accepts `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset` (default 0)
to page through the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the newest (default 0).

200.description: Manual adjustments recorded for this supplier

post.summary: Record a manual payable adjustment on a supplier's account.
post.description:
Writes `adjustment_in` or `adjustment_out` without touching any wallet.
Both directions require the balance to stay `>= 0`: an adjustment may load
an opening payable or correct a balance, never create or consume advance
credit.

409.description: The supplier account is busy, retry

422.description: Blank note, invalid amount, or adjustment crossing zero

post.summary:
Record refunded advance credit returned by a supplier through a wallet
inflow.
post.description:
One request, one transaction: a `supplier_account_refund` inflow enters the
payment method's wallet and a `credit_refund` entry moves the supplier's
balance toward zero. Refused unless `amount <= min(unapplied_credit, -balance)`.
An optional idempotency key returns the first refund with `200` instead of
booking the inflow twice.

200.description: Existing credit refund returned for a repeated idempotency key; nothing was written

201.description: Credit refund recorded: wallet inflow and ledger entry written together

409.description: Busy supplier account, or idempotency key already used by another entry kind

422.description: Unknown or inactive payment method, blank note, invalid amount, or amount exceeding refundable credit

post.summary: Soft deactivation. Idempotent. Requires a zero account position (409 otherwise).

409.description: Open account position or account busy

get.summary: Payment write log for one supplier, newest first.
get.description:
Accepts `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset` (default 0)
to page through the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Entries to skip from the newest (default 0).

post.summary: Record a payment against a supplier's account.
post.description:
One request, one transaction: money leaves the payment method's wallet as a
`supplier_account_payment` movement carrying the supplier and the method,
and the supplier's ledger records one `payment` entry linked to it.
Allocations are explicit — the server never invents them — and any
unallocated remainder becomes unapplied advance credit with the supplier.
An optional idempotency key makes a retry return the first payment with
`200` instead of paying twice.

200.description: Existing payment returned for a repeated idempotency key; nothing was written

201.description: Payment recorded: wallet outflow and ledger entry written together

404.description: Unknown supplier, or an allocation names an unknown purchase

409.description: Busy supplier account, or idempotency key already used by another entry kind

422.description: Unknown or inactive payment method, invalid amount, overlong idempotency key, or invalid allocations

get.summary: List every user, ordered by email. Only `owner`.

403.description: Role does not permit managing users

post.summary: Create a user. Only `owner`.

403.description: Role does not permit managing users

409.description: Email is already registered

put.description:
No current password is requested: the owner cannot know it. Every previous
session of the target is revoked atomically; when the owner resets their
own password, a rotated `session` cookie is emitted.

204.description: Password reset, target sessions revoked (and rotated Set-Cookie emitted on self-reset)

403.description: Role does not permit managing users

get.summary: List wallets with their calculated balance.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description:
Include deactivated rows. The settings screen needs them so a wallet can
be brought back; the POS does not.

post.summary: Create a wallet (a cash box, a bank account).

409.description: Name is already in use

409.description: Name is already in use

get.summary: Movements of one wallet, newest first.
get.description:
Accepts `limit` (default 50, clamped to 1..=200) and `offset` (default 0)
to page through the wallet ledger.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of movements to return (default 50, clamped to 1..=200).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Movements to skip from the newest (default 0).

post.summary: Record money leaving or entering a wallet by hand.
post.description:
`sale_payment`, `sale_refund`, `account_payment` and
`account_payment_refund` are rejected with 422: money that belongs to a
sale or a customer's account enters or leaves the ledger only through the
flow that also writes its counterpart, never by hand.

AccountStatementEntryResponse.description:
One ledger line in a customer's account statement, with the balance right
after it.

amount.description: Signed effect on the balance: positive grows debt, negative shrinks it.

running_balance.description: Customer's running balance immediately after this entry.

AdjustmentDirection.description: Direction of a manual debt adjustment.

amount.description:
Signed effect on the balance: positive for `adjustment_in`, negative
for `adjustment_out`.

adjustment_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the adjustment.

balance.description: The customer's balance after the adjustment. Always `>= 0.00`.

AgingBucketsResponse.description:
Open sale debt split into aging buckets from each sale's `completed_at`
date (`0-30`, `31-60`, `61-90`, `90+`). No due date in this delivery.

CollectReceiptRequest.description:
A collection: money that arrived, and the sales it pays.

The allocations are the operator's decision; the server never invents one
and never applies the remainder — that remainder becomes the customer's
usable credit exactly by carrying no row.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key. A repeated collection with the same key returns
the first receipt with `200` instead of collecting twice.

on_account.description:
Portion of the purchase total charged to the supplier's account instead
of paid upfront from a wallet (defaults to `0.00`).

CompleteSaleRequest.description:
How the sale is paid. Required: a sale never closes without saying where the
money went.

on_account.description:
Part of the total charged to the customer's account instead of
collected at the till. Optional and defaults to 0; never negative and
at most two decimals. The payments plus this amount must equal the
total the server calculated, and a positive amount needs an active
customer on the draft whose credit limit still fits it.

credit_applied.description:
Unapplied supplier advance credit automatically allocated to this
purchase upon completion (`"0.00"` when none applied).

How much of the on-account part the customer's available credit paid
automatically: `on_account - credit_applied` is the debt the sale
actually added. Money with two decimals, like `total`; `"0.00"` for
a sale that never used the account.

payment_movement_ids.description:
One movement per payment, so the client can follow the money into its
wallets without a second request.

CreateCreditNoteRequest.description: A return. The total is not sent: the server calculates it.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key. A repeated create with the same key and sale
returns the first note instead of issuing another one.

reason.description: Why the goods came back. Required, and kept on the document.

credit_limit.description:
Optional credit limit: absent or `null` means unlimited, `0` means
cash only. Never negative, at most two decimals.

tax_id.description: Optional and unique when present. An empty string means "no document".

price.description:
Documented as `string` although the server also accepts numbers:
`rust_decimal` deserializes both, but the frontend contract—and the only
one preserving precision—is the string. See `docs/api-contract.md`.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key unique per purchase. Repeating a request with the
same key returns the original return with `200` instead of writing a
duplicate.

reason.description: Why the goods are being returned. Required and stored on the document.

surplus_mode.description:
How any already-paid surplus above the purchase's open payable should
be handled (`wallet_refund` or `supplier_credit`). Defaults to
`wallet_refund`.

credit_limit.description:
Optional credit limit: absent or `null` means unlimited, `0` means cash
only. Never negative, at most two decimals.

tax_id.description: Optional and unique when present. A blank string means "no document".

CreditNoteLineRequest.description: One line to return. The price is not sent: it is the one charged on the sale.

sale_id.description: The sale being corrected. The sale itself never changes.

total.description: Calculated by the server from the returned quantities.

balance.description: The customer's balance after the refund. Never positive after a refund.

refund_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the refund.

unapplied_credit.description: Usable credit remaining after the refund.

wallet_movement_id.description:
The `account_payment_refund` movement that carried the money out of the
wallet.

CreditableLineResponse.description:
A charged line, with the quantity already credited and what can still come
back.

CustomerAccountEntryKind.description:
Why the customer's account moved.

An enum, like `WalletMovementKind`, for the same reason: a new kind always
arrives with a writer, a validation and a screen — that is, with code.

CustomerAccountResponse.description:
Complete account statement for one customer: entries oldest first with a
running balance, current position, and every sale with debt.

balance.description: Current signed balance. Positive: the customer owes. Negative: credit.

entries.description:
Ledger entries oldest first, each carrying the running balance after it
(default 100 per page, clamped to 1..=500). `entries_total` is the whole
ledger either way.

entries_total.description: Ledger entries in the whole statement, not just this page.

outstanding_total.description: Sum of what every open sale still owes.

unapplied_credit.description: Collected money not yet allocated to a sale or refunded (`U`).

limit.description: Page size actually applied (the request defaults to 50, is capped at 200).

offset.description: Offset of `items[0]` in the filtered set.

total.description:
How many customers the filters match in total, ignoring the page. A client
needs this to tell a full page from the last one.

available_credit.description: Collected money not yet allocated to a sale or refunded (`U`).

balance.description:
Current account balance derived from the customer's debt ledger.
Positive means the customer owes money; negative means credit in their
favour.

credit_limit.description:
`null` means no limit (the default), `"0.00"` means cash only. Money as
a string with its cents, like every other amount in the tree.

tax_id.description:
`null` when the customer was registered without a document, which is a
normal case: a walk-in buyer is still a customer.

reused.description: `true` if the existing open draft was reused.

kind.description:
`expense`, `adjustment_in` or `adjustment_out`. `sale_payment`,
`sale_refund`, `account_payment`, `account_payment_refund` and
`purchase_payment` are rejected: that money is recorded by charging or
returning a sale, collecting or refunding a customer's account, or
completing a purchase, not by hand.

signed_quantity.description:
Signed quantity: what the client needs to show the stock effect without
replicating the sign rule.

OutstandingPurchaseResponse.description:
One completed purchase that still has an open payable on the supplier's
account.

OutstandingSaleResponse.description: One sale that still owes money on the customer's account.

PayableSupplierResponse.description:
One supplier with an open account position (`balance != 0` or
`unapplied_credit != 0`).

PayablesAgingBucketsResponse.description:
Open purchase payables split into aging buckets from each purchase's
`completed_at` timestamp (`0-30`, `31-60`, `61-90`, `90+`).

PayablesResponse.description:
Portfolio-wide payables report across every supplier with an open account
position.

items_total.description: Suppliers in the whole report, not just this page.

wallet_id.description:
The wallet this method pays into. The UI shows its name so nobody
charges into the wrong account without noticing.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 error body. Same shape for every status code.

status.description: HTTP status, repeated in the body for clients that do not read headers.

title.description: Human-readable, stable summary of the problem.

type.description: URI identifying the problem type. Currently always `about:blank`.

ProductKind.description: A catalog item may or may not track stock.

limit.description: Page size actually applied (the request defaults to 50, is capped at 200).

offset.description: Offset of `items[0]` in the filtered set.

total.description:
How many products the filters match in total, ignoring the page. A client
needs this to tell a full page from the last one.

low_stock.description: `null` when not applicable (service) or no threshold is configured.

price.description:
String, not number: a JSON `float` loses precision for money and
fractional quantities. The client parses it as a decimal.

stock.description: `null` for services: not zero, but "not applicable".

reused.description: `true` if the operator's existing open draft was reused.

supplier_name.description: Live registry name while draft; frozen snapshot once completed.

PurchaseReturnLineRequest.description:
One line to return to the supplier. Unit cost is never sent by the client:
the server uses the frozen cost from the linked purchase line.

PurchaseReturnRefundResponse.description: One wallet inflow written when `surplus_mode = wallet_refund`.

credit_granted.description: Portion of `total` left as unapplied supplier credit (`surplus_mode = supplier_credit`).

debt_cancelled.description: Portion of `total` that cancelled open payable debt on the purchase.

total.description: Server-calculated total from the returned quantities and frozen unit costs.

PurchaseReturnsSummaryResponse.description: Returnable state and issued returns for one purchase.

purchase_outstanding.description: Current open payable on this purchase (cancelled first by any new return).

wallet_refundable_capacity.description: Maximum paid surplus that can still be refunded to wallets for this purchase.

ReceiptAllocationRequest.description: Which sale one slice of the collected money pays.

ReceiptAllocationResponse.description: One allocated sale with what it still owes after the receipt.

outstanding.description: The sale's outstanding amount after this receipt's allocation.

ReceiptLogAllocationResponse.description: One allocation inside the receipt write log.

allocated_total.description: Sum of allocations pointing at this receipt.

balance.description:
The customer's balance after the collection. Positive: they still
owe. Negative: they hold money in their favour.

receipt_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the collection.

unapplied_credit.description:
Money collected that no allocation consumed yet, and no refund has
returned: what the next sale on account may consume.

wallet_movement_id.description: The `account_payment` movement that carried the money into the wallet.

ReceivableCustomerResponse.description:
One customer with an open account position (`balance != 0` or
`unapplied_credit != 0`).

ReceivablesResponse.description:
Portfolio-wide receivables report across every customer with an open
account position.

items_total.description: Customers in the whole report, not just this page.

RecordAdjustmentRequest.description: A manual adjustment against a customer's debt ledger. Touches no wallet.

note.description: Why the balance was adjusted. Required and non-blank.

RecordSupplierAdjustmentRequest.description: A manual adjustment against a supplier's payables ledger. Touches no wallet.

note.description: Why the balance was adjusted. Required and non-blank.

RecordSupplierPaymentRequest.description:
A payment to a supplier: money leaving a wallet, and the completed
purchases it pays.

Allocations are explicit and never invented by the server; any unallocated
remainder becomes unapplied advance credit with the supplier.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key. A repeated payment with the same key returns the
first payment with `200` instead of paying twice.

RefundCreditRequest.description: A credit refund: money handed back to a customer who holds usable credit.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key. A repeated refund with the same key returns the
first refund with `200` instead of handing the money back twice.

note.description: Why the money is being handed back. Required and non-blank.

RefundSupplierCreditRequest.description:
A credit refund: unapplied advance credit returned by a supplier into a
wallet.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional retry key. A repeated refund with the same key returns the
first refund with `200` instead of booking the inflow twice.

note.description: Why the supplier refunded the advance credit. Required and non-blank.

ReturnablePurchaseLineResponse.description: One purchased line with cumulative returned and remaining returnable quantities.

SaleCreditNotesResponse.description:
The sale's credits: its charged lines, the money still refundable, and
the notes already issued.

refundable_total.description:
The money allowance create still enforces: `sale_total` minus
`refunded_total`. Once it reaches zero, further notes are refused
even if units remain.

quantity.description:
Quantity as a string: `numeric(12,3)` does not fit in a float without
losing precision for fractional quantities.

total.description: Total completed sales, not just the ones on this page.

SalePaymentRequest.description: One payment of the charge. A sale can be paid with several.

amount.description:
Positive. The sum of every payment must equal the total the server
calculated, or the charge is rejected with 422.

customer_id.description: The customer the sale is charged to, `null` for an anonymous sale.

customer_name.description:
The live registry name while the sale is a draft; the snapshot frozen
at completion once closed, so a later rename changes nothing.

total.description: Calculated on the server. The client displays it, not decides it.

SetPurchaseSupplierRequest.description:
Attaches a supplier to the draft, or clears it.

`supplier_id` must be present: clearing is an explicit `null`, and an
omitted field is rejected (`422`) instead of detaching the supplier silently.

supplier_id.description: Supplier to attach to the draft, or `null` to clear it.

SetSaleCustomerRequest.description:
Attaches a customer to the draft, or clears it.

`customer_id` must be present: clearing is an explicit `null`, and an omitted
field is rejected instead of being read as "clear". A truncated payload
would otherwise detach a customer silently, and the cashier would see it only
on the printed ticket.

customer_id.description: The customer to attach, or `null` to leave the sale anonymous.

SupplierAccountResponse.description:
Complete account statement for one supplier: entries oldest first with a
running balance, current position, and every purchase with open payable.

balance.description:
Current signed balance. Positive: we owe the supplier. Negative: we
hold advance credit with them.

entries.description:
Ledger entries oldest first, each carrying the running balance after it
(default 100 per page, clamped to 1..=500). `entries_total` is the whole
ledger either way.

entries_total.description: Ledger entries in the whole statement, not just this page.

outstanding_total.description: Sum of what every open purchase still owes.

unapplied_credit.description: Paid money not yet allocated to a purchase or refunded.

SupplierAccountStatementEntryResponse.description:
One ledger line in a supplier's account statement, with the running balance
right after it.

amount.description:
Signed effect on the balance: positive grows what we owe, negative
shrinks it.

running_balance.description: Supplier's running balance immediately after this entry.

SupplierAdjustmentDirection.description: Direction of a manual payable adjustment.

amount.description:
Signed effect on the balance: positive for `adjustment_in`, negative
for `adjustment_out`.

adjustment_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the adjustment.

balance.description: The supplier's balance after the adjustment. Always `>= 0.00`.
The supplier's balance after the refund. Never positive after a refund.

refund_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the refund.

unapplied_credit.description: Unapplied advance credit remaining after the refund.

wallet_movement_id.description:
The `supplier_account_refund` movement that carried the money into the
wallet.

limit.description: Page size actually applied (defaults to 50, capped at 200).

offset.description: Offset of `items[0]` in the filtered set.

total.description: Total matching suppliers across all pages.

SupplierPaymentAllocationRequest.description: Which completed purchase one slice of a supplier payment applies to.

SupplierPaymentAllocationResponse.description: One allocated purchase with what it still owes after this payment.

outstanding.description: The purchase's outstanding payable after this payment's allocation.

SupplierPaymentLogAllocationResponse.description: One purchase allocation inside the supplier payment write log.

allocated_total.description: Sum of allocations pointing at this payment.

balance.description:
The supplier's balance after the payment. Positive: we still owe the
supplier. Negative: we hold advance credit with them.

payment_id.description: The ledger entry that recorded the payment.

unapplied_credit.description: Money paid to the supplier not yet allocated to a purchase or refunded.

wallet_movement_id.description:
The `supplier_account_payment` movement that carried the money out of
the wallet.

available_credit.description: Money paid to the supplier not yet allocated to a purchase or refunded (`U`).

balance.description:
Current account balance derived from `supplier_account_entries`.
Positive means we owe the supplier; negative means advance credit held.

tax_id.description: `null` when the supplier was registered without a tax document.

SurplusMode.description:
How an already-paid surplus (the portion of a return that exceeds the
purchase's open payable debt) should be settled.

credit_limit.description:
The one clearable field: absent leaves the limit untouched, an explicit
`null` returns the customer to unlimited, a value sets it. The double
`Option` keeps the three cases apart the same way `PUT
/sales/{id}/customer` keeps attach and clear apart.

tax_id.description: `null` means "leave the document as it is", never "clear it".

wallet_id.description:
Moving a method to another wallet changes where **future** money lands.
Nothing already recorded moves: every movement keeps the wallet it hit.

credit_limit.description:
Tri-state: omitted leaves the limit untouched, explicit `null` clears
it back to unlimited, and a value sets the cap.

tax_id.description: `null` means "leave the document as it is", never "clear it".

WalletMovementKind.description:
Why money moved.

This is an enum while payment methods are rows, and the asymmetry is the
point: a new method is business data the operator creates, but a new kind
always arrives with a writer, a validation and a screen — that is, with code.

amount.description: Always positive; the kind carries the sign.

payment_method_id.description:
Set for `sale_payment`, `sale_refund`, `account_payment`, `account_payment_refund`,
`purchase_payment`, `supplier_account_payment`, or `supplier_account_refund`:
which payment method was used.

purchase_id.description: Set only for a `purchase_payment`: which purchase paid out this money.

sale_id.description: Set only for a `sale_payment` or `sale_refund`: which sale moved this money.

signed_amount.description:
The wallet's effect of this movement, so the client does not replicate
the sign rule.

balance.description:
Calculated: the signed sum of the wallet's movements, as a string with
two decimals. `"-1500.00"` is a valid answer — expenses can exceed what
the wallet holds.
